Synopsis:
OM available only for Avatar Wyll. He arrived at the Grove and meets with Asharak and the training kids. Now he can boost the kids' spirits with a story.

- DEN_TrainingKids_OM_Wyll_AOM.json: OM available only for Avatar Wyll. He arrived at the Grove and meets with Asharak and the training kids. Now he can boost the kids' spirits with a story.
- DEN_Thieflings_Trainer.json: The scene takes place at a makeshift training area where Asharak is overseeing a group of child trainees; he recognized the player earlier at the gates and knows they can fight. Asharak asks the player—sometimes quietly, out of earshot of the kids—to say a few words, tell a story, or otherwise inspire the children; the player can respond with a rousing speech, a savage roar, or darker humor. Asharak should sound weary and a little sad in his lines: he resents having to teach children to fight and doesn't relish this role. This is an optional, non‑critical interaction; depending on game flags some trainees might not be present.
- Wyll_Recruitment_PostEA.json: Post EA dialog version.Initial dialogue with Wyll. In most cases, this will involve him training a tiefling child before the player breaks in, and you discover you were both on the mind flayer ship. Wyll comes across as a big-time hero, and wants help killing goblins. He is called the Blade of Frontiers by most.
- CAMP_Ravengard.json: Default Ravengard dialogue. Depending on the path, Ravengard may urge you to save the city, and if Wyll is in party, will offer the quest to go to the Wyrmway. Wyll's endgame state is detremined here: He may become a Duke, the Blade of Avernus, or remain the Blade of Frontiers

retrieved_synopses: OM available only for Avatar Wyll. He arrived at the Grove and meets with Asharak and the training kids. Now he can boost the kids' spirits with a story.

The scene takes place at a makeshift training area where Asharak is overseeing a group of child trainees; he recognized the player earlier at the gates and knows they can fight. Asharak asks the player—sometimes quietly, out of earshot of the kids—to say a few words, tell a story, or otherwise inspire the children; the player can respond with a rousing speech, a savage roar, or darker humor. Asharak should sound weary and a little sad in his lines: he resents having to teach children to fight and doesn't relish this role. This is an optional, non‑critical interaction; depending on game flags some trainees might not be present.

Post EA dialog version.Initial dialogue with Wyll. In most cases, this will involve him training a tiefling child before the player breaks in, and you discover you were both on the mind flayer ship. Wyll comes across as a big-time hero, and wants help killing goblins. He is called the Blade of Frontiers by most.

Default Ravengard dialogue. Depending on the path, Ravengard may urge you to save the city, and if Wyll is in party, will offer the quest to go to the Wyrmway. Wyll's endgame state is detremined here: He may become a Duke, the Blade of Avernus, or remain the Blade of Frontiers
Default dialogue when speaking to Wyll during exploration.
context: This optional moment appears only for the Avatar Wyll. He has arrived at the Grove and been brought before Asharak, who runs a makeshift training area of child trainees and already recognized the PC’s ability at the gates. Asharak, weary and resigned about teaching kids to fight, asks Wyll—quietly and out of earshot of the others—to say a few words or tell a story to lift their spirits, noting the goblin threat. Wyll is treated as a heroic figure (the “Blade of Frontiers”) and responds with boastful, larger‑than‑life tales to entertain the children; depending on flags some trainees might not be present and the exchange is non‑critical.
